intro: Lesson 20: Living the akhlaq: amanah (trust). To understand what amanah means and how Muslims keep trusts in daily life

questions.q: Explain why time is an amanah.
questions.a: Allah gave us time and will ask how we used it; wasting it is not keeping the trust.
questions.model: Point: our time belongs to Allah's gift. Evidence: Allah swears by time in Surah al-'Asr (103:1-3). Explain: we will be asked how we used it, so we use it in good. Link: an hour of homework done well is keeping a trust.

questions.q: In the portal response box, write a short talk for the Youth Club: 'Amanah in a teenager's life'. Use three examples and two pieces of evidence. Start: 'Brothers and sisters, amanah is ...'
questions.a: Talk with three examples (phone, secrets, time) and evidence (4:58, 103:1-3, al-Amin)
questions.model: Teacher writes the opening: 'Brothers and sisters, amanah is anything placed in our care, and Allah commands us to return it (4:58).'

questions.q: how is the online world full of trusts?
questions.a: Passwords, private messages, photos of others, group chats.

questions.q: why did the Prophet ﷺ return the Quraysh's trusts even as they plotted against him?
questions.a: Amanah is kept even with enemies; it is a duty to Allah.

questions.q: Reading a friend's messages without asking is ...
Back to our ponder: what can you do with the borrowed phone?
questions.a: Only what the owner agreed: it is an amanah.
